correctness.rationale: For strictly positive L,T,W, the product of Hurwitz-stable quadratic probability polynomials is Hurwitz stable. Strict Hermite--Biehler interlaces the negative roots of the even polynomial P and odd polynomial Q, and the ratio Q/P has positive residues. Normalizing its partial fractions gives an exact convex mixture of the n Bernoulli-deletion distributions of P/P(1). The convolution identity s(k)=(1-p)d(k)+pd(k-1) proves every deletion mode lies in [a-1,b] if the full Bernoulli sum has modal interval [a,b]. Unimodality therefore confines mixture modes to the same interval. Boundary probability vectors follow by compactness of n Bernoulli parameters and mixture weights; the proof does not rely on continuity of argmax sets. The resulting parity-score distance is at most 3/2, is 1/2 if P has one mode, and is exactly attained by the explicit two-trial polynomial G(w)=(w+3w^2)(1+w^2)/8. The standalone checker completed 52686 admissible exact integer-grid cases, including all tied and zero-probability cases on the quarter grid for n<=4. Crucial infinite steps are analytical; finite tests are only corroboration.

originality.rationale: Direct statement-by-statement comparison of the complete Broadie--Petkova article finds only the 5/2 general modal bound, not the attained 3/2 optimum or the unique-integer-mode half-step localization. The Hermite--Biehler root-interlacing property and separate Poisson-binomial modes were already known and are not claimed as discoveries. The additional positive-residue Bernoulli-deletion mixture and its modal-localization implication are proved here. Searches of mathematical records for equivalent root, coefficient, deletion, mode and parity formulations located no covering statement; a literature search alone cannot certify priority.

value.rationale: The model is a natural exact win/tie/loss sum with an explicit quantitative 5/2 modal-distance bound central to the source paper. The new 3/2 bound is both sharp and forty percent smaller, and it holds for all independent nonidentical summands including zero-probability outcome faces, without bounded n. More structurally, it proves that a unique even conditional mode pins every odd conditional mode to an adjacent half-step; the only larger cross-parity gap is tied to an adjacent two-point integer modal interval. A complete exact extremal classification and explanation are mathematically useful and non-routine, not an arbitrary finite tabulation or a relabeling.
